question: What will the top score on the ARC Prize 2026 – ARC-AGI-3 Kaggle public leaderboard be on September 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Kaggle public leaderboards are monotone non-decreasing (best submission per team is retained), so the floor is effectively today's 7.51 and the whole question is how much is added in 10 days. Reference class: ~10-day top-score changes in long-running ARC Prize Kaggle competitions mid-to-late in the run, where most windows are incremental and a minority contain discrete technique jumps; that decomposition puts the median near x1.10-1.20 (~8.3-9.0) with a right tail from a repeat of the August regime break that took 1.86 to 7.51 in six weeks. Two forces push down: each marginal point is harder at a higher absolute level, submissions are slow (long agent runtimes, daily caps), and Milestone #2 standings are measured Sept 30, giving strong teams a reason to hold their best entry back past Sept 17. Two push up: the top three are clustered at 7.51/6.66/6.43, which reads like a shared technique diffusing and invites leapfrogging, and the pre-milestone ramp is already underway. Evidence is thin — I could not read the live leaderboard directly and rely on secondhand confirmation of 7.51 — so I stay close to the base rate. No market prices this contract; the Manifold ARC-AGI-3 question resolves off the ARC Prize model-eval harness (GPT-6 Astra at 62.7%), not the offline compute-capped Kaggle LB, so it is evidence about the benchmark's headroom, not an anchor for this number. Downside escape below 6 has no mechanism (even deleting the leader leaves 6.43); upside escape past 25 needs a ~3.3x in 10 days, priced small but nonzero given August precedent.

calls.reasoning: Verified the live Kaggle public leaderboard via a text proxy: top is Tufa Labs 11.04, then 7.91 / 7.63 / 7.51, with the whole top-15 submitting within the last day. That 11.04 is a hard floor for Sept 17 (a running max cannot fall; even removing the top team leaves ~7.9, still inside the range), so the whole question is how much the max climbs in 10.6 days. Reference class: this competition's own ~11-day windows in 2026. Whole-run average log growth is 0.023/day (x1.27 over the horizon = 14.0), the Jul 23 -> Sep 7 burst is 0.033/day (x1.42 = 15.7), and the May 22 -> Jul 23 plateau was 0.008/day (x1.09 = 12.0). I centre near 14.4 -- the run-average rate, deliberately below the recent burst, because the max is driven by discrete leader jumps and Tufa's 11.04 is a fresh outlier 40% clear of #2, which historically buys a pause. Counter-argument for higher: 2,860 teams, Milestone #2 on Sept 30 with $25K/$10K/$2.5K, an open-source requirement that propagates leading solutions through public forks, no saturation constraint at 11%, and a public split of only ~50% of test data that rewards leaderboard tuning; the last 10 days alone ran roughly x1.8-2.5. Counter-argument for lower: ~12% weight that nobody clears 11.04 at all. Evidence is thin on August intra-month datapoints -- the Wayback proxy 403'd on every snapshot -- so the growth rate between Jul 23 and Sep 3 is interpolated, not observed, and I stayed nearer the base rate for it. 8% priced above 25 for a second Tufa-style step-change plus fast fork propagation; no p_below_lower because reaching 6 would require mass disqualification of the entire top four and permanent leaderboard discontinuation annuls rather than resolves.

calls.reconciliation: Central dispute was FACTUAL: current top-of-board. Runs 1 and 3 could not load the JS-rendered Kaggle leaderboard and anchored on the background's stale 'early September 7.51'; Run 2 reported Tufa Labs 11.04. I fetched the live leaderboard myself through a text proxy and got Run 2's rows exactly (11.04 / 7.91 / 7.63 / 7.51 / 5.49 / 5.43 / 5.33), with the background's three named teams all still present and only higher - consistent with a real snapshot. I separately fetched the Kaggle discussion index and confirmed every forum thread Run 2 cited exists at the stated age, so its dossier is corroborated rather than confabulated. A web search for the 11.04 figure returned nothing (expected; no outlet reports Kaggle boards), and my attempt at a dated August Medium snapshot 403'd, so the Jul 23 -> Sep 7 velocity stays interpolated. Because a Kaggle public LB retains each team's best submission, 11.04 is a hard monotone floor and the entire question is the 10.6-day increment. On the JUDGMENT axis I do not follow Run 2 to the run-average rate: the trailing burst window terminates on a fresh record (selection bias), and extending 0.023/day to the Nov 2 close would finish near 40, far past the prior season's 27.64 public endpoint, so I apply ~1.25-1.30x and center at 13.8. I also reject the Runs 1/3 withholding-until-Milestone-2 argument on evidence: the live board shows the entire top 15 submitting within 4 days, most within 17h, and the leader at 130 entries. Zero-movement mass set to ~13% (below Runs 1/3's 20-25%) given an active leader and a chasing pack at 7.5-7.9. 8% above 25 because the last ~5 days alone delivered roughly the required 2.3x once, plus documented harness-config step changes propagating through public forks. 1% below 6 requires simultaneous removal of the top four (the mostik.ai 12-of-8-members eligibility thread is real but unresolved and mostik sits 4th, so it cannot lower the max); permanent LB discontinuation annuls rather than resolves. Market check: I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmaker contract resolving off this Kaggle public leaderboard - none found; all three runs agree, and the only nearby Manifold markets resolve off the ARC Prize verified-model harness (GPT-6 Astra 62.7%), a different instrument, different threshold and no Sep 17 date, so a near-miss and not an anchor.
